title: Generalizing Thermal Transport in High-Contrast Metamaterials through Interfacial Fresnel Reflection
authors: Seung Hyeon Ham, Yu Min Kim, In Hyeok Choi, Jeong Woo Han
abstract: The rapid growth of generative AI has intensified the need for efficient heat dissipation in large-scale data centers. To control heat flow, thermal metamaterials with layered structures have been widely used, which impart the anisotropic properties of thermal conductivities. However, the conventional effective medium approximation (EMA) often fails to provide accurate predictions in systems with a high thermal conductivity contrast between adjacent layers embedded in a background medium. Here, we generalize the EMA by introducing two corrective coefficients that extend its validity to regimes where the conventional EMA was previously inapplicable, i.e., high-contrast thermal metamaterials with the background medium. Notably, one of these coefficients that we proposed has the same mathematical form as the Fresnel reflection coefficient in optics. This allows us to interpret the "reflection-like" behavior of heat flow as it penetrates adjacent layers with high thermal contrast. Our findings suggest that heat diffusion, traditionally viewed as a purely dissipative process, can be understood intuitively through the framework of ray optics.
summary: This paper improves the theoretical modeling of heat transport in layered metamaterials by generalizing the Effective Medium Approximation (EMA). The authors introduce corrective terms, one mimicking optical reflection, to account for high thermal conductivity contrasts and background media effects. This allows for more accurate prediction of heat flow direction in technologically relevant thermal structures.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for accurate thermal modeling in high-contrast metamaterials, particularly for applications like data center heat dissipation.
main_result: The authors generalize the Effective Medium Approximation (EMA) by introducing corrective coefficients, allowing the model to accurately predict heat flow behavior where conventional EMA fails due to high conductivity contrast or background media effects.
method: The study develops a generalized EMA by incorporating two corrective coefficients: one analogous to Fresnel reflection and another inspired by series electronic circuits.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a layered thermal metamaterial composed of alternating layers ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2$) embedded in a background medium ($ eta$), governed by Fourier's law.
key_observables: Heat flow bending angle ($\varphi$) and its deviation ($\Delta\varphi$) from conventional EMA predictions.
important_parameters: Thermal conductivities ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2,  eta$) and the conductivity ratio ($r = \kappa_1 / \kappa_2$).
main_assumptions: The conventional EMA fails when the thermal conductivity contrast is high or when the background medium significantly influences heat flow.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the heat flow bending angle under various conditions and plot the deviation ($\Delta\varphi$) of the heat-flow bending angle as a function of conductivity ratio, layer number, and background medium conductivity.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of the conventional EMA in high-contrast thermal systems. It then proposes and derives the generalized EMA using two corrective coefficients. Finally, it validates the generalized model through numerical simulations comparing results against the conventional EMA.
why_interesting: While focused on classical heat transfer, the mathematical analogy drawn between heat flow and optical reflection (Fresnel coefficients) provides a powerful, transferable framework for analyzing energy transport in complex, structured media, which has parallels in quantum wave phenomena.
